title: Firebase MCP Server
summary: Run the Firebase CLI's built-in MCP server so your agent can work with Firestore, Auth, rules and hosting in your Firebase project.
description: The Firebase CLI ships an MCP server of its own. Started with firebase-tools mcp, it gives the agent tools for projects and apps, Firestore documents and indexes, Auth users, security rules, Remote Config, Cloud Functions logs, deploys and a search over Google's developer docs.
It uses the same login as the Firebase CLI, so run firebase login first. You can narrow it to a few feature groups with the --only flag and point it at a project folder with --dir.
useWhen: Query Firestore to see why a document is missing a field
Review and validate security rules before a deploy
Read recent Cloud Functions logs after an error report
Look up a user in Auth while reproducing a sign-in bug

mcp.name: firebase
access: Reads and writes Firestore, Auth and Storage data in the project you are logged in to
Uses your Firebase CLI credentials and runs on your machine

example.prompt: In Firestore, list the 3 newest documents in orders and tell me which ones lack a customerId.
example.result: orders/o_9921 and orders/o_9920 have customerId. orders/o_9919 has no customerId field, and its createdAt is from the older checkout flow.

faq.question: Do I need a service account key?
faq.answer: No. It reuses your Firebase CLI login or Application Default Credentials, and the page documents no environment variables.

faq.question: How do I limit what it can do?
faq.answer: The --only flag turns on just the feature groups you list. Leave out groups you do not need, and use a staging project when testing.

access: Acts with your Firebase CLI credentials on the selected project
Can change Firestore data, Auth users and deploy resources
